rows.title: Role-filtered party pickers on one page
rows.detail: Makes each live-animals party picker, and the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, offer only the organisation's addresses saved for that party's role, all on one page, so a trader is never offered a destination address as a place of origin. An address saved for several roles shows on each of their pickers, an address saved as an exporter shows on the consignor picker, and an address saved with no role shows on every picker until it is given one, so nobody loses an address on a guess. Both frontends' stub books get roles on their canned records, so stub mode filters as the real thing does. Because each picker now lists one role's addresses, the list fits on one page and the restatement of the choice above it is no longer needed. Search stays the server search behind the submitting search button; filtering as the trader types waits on design in its own row.
acceptanceCriteria: On the compose stack, an address saved for the consignee role only is listed on the consignee picker, and each of the place of origin, consignor, importer and place of destination pickers lists only the addresses saved for its own role (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-070, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-098; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-047)

The consignor picker lists the organisation's addresses saved for the consignor role together with those saved for the exporter role, and the roles and addresses page's party sections are Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-064, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-137; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116)

An address saved for several roles is listed on the picker of every party whose role it carries, so one company can be chosen as both the consignee and the importer (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-065)

On the compose stack, the high-risk plants consignor picker lists the addresses saved for the consignor role and the high-risk plants place of destination picker lists those saved for the place of destination role (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-040; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-006)

An address saved with no role at all is listed on all five animals pickers and on both high-risk plants pickers, on the compose stack and in stub mode (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-051; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-040)

In stub mode, each animals picker and each high-risk plants picker lists the canned records that carry its role together with any canned record that has no role, so the five animals pickers do not all list the same records (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-168, repo-frontend-p9-169, repo-frontend-p9-170; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-064, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-083, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-092)

Each animals picker and each high-risk plants picker lists every address it offers on one page: between the search box and the save buttons the page shows the results heading, the results count and one table holding every address for the role, however many the role has (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-052, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-056, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-057; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-007, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-021)

Reopening an animals or high-risk plants picker for a party that already has an address shows that address as the checked row of the one-page table, and the page shows nothing between the search box and the results heading (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-050, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-055; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-017)

Submitting a search in either frontend's picker shows the picker again with the role's matching addresses on one page, keeps the search text in the box and saves nothing (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-054; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-066; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-055)

rows.gate: Look at role filtering on the compose stack and in stub mode, in both frontends, before the rows that rest on it build: a role-carrying record appears only on its roles' pickers, a record with no role appears on every picker, the list is one page, and the server search narrows it. The same-as row, the live filter row and the germinal set's copy of the pickers build on this.
rows.notes: Re-drafted on this re-distil from existing row inc-087; no frontend requirement behind it changed in substance. Combines role filtering in the pickers (each frontend asking by role, the role-less fallback, stub roles) with one-page listing and dropping the restatement of the choice, because c-094 rules they land together: one page is only sensible once it is one role's addresses, and the restatement only existed to carry a selection across pages. CHANGE ON THIS RE-DISTIL: req-611 (the address book holding roles on the record and listing an organisation's addresses for one role, unpaginated, excluding deleted records) has left this row. Its code is addressbook:src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/addressbook/address, which the split-off address-book theme owns, and that theme's own row inc-059 already builds the typed record there (req-1256); main's Address.java is still documented as 'an untyped, organisation-owned address-book entry' and AddressRequest refuses a type. So req-611 is listed in this draft's splitOff for the address-book branch to pick up, the addressbook repo key has left this row's repos, and the criterion about the address book's own role-scoped list has gone with it. This row therefore waits on the address-book branch delivering roles and the role-scoped list: the combiner should record that as an externalDependsOn on shared/design-release-2-1/themes/address-book (the consignment-parties theme already depends on address-book, so the landing order holds). It also fixes the consignment-parties theme's wrong touch addressbook:.../addressbook/service, which holds only EmfMetricsPublisher.java: this row builds nothing in the address book, so that touch should go. The CDP wording of the role-less criterion has been narrowed to the compose stack and stub mode, the environments this row's repos actually run in; in CDP every record saved before roles land has no role, which is why the fallback matters, but a build cannot observe CDP. c-100: DR1's typed-record block is lifted, in the address book, not here. c-101: role-less records show on every picker until given a role, never filtered on a guess. Both frontends' address-book services stay read-only (c-106, req-618). Giving a record its roles through the INS address book's add and edit pages is the address-book and party-address-add-and-edit areas' work; the role-carrying records these criteria use are set-up for a one-page assertion, which the test rules allow. The animals stub book mirrors the tests repo's e2e address-book fixture record for record, so the fixture needs the same roles; that fixture (tests:domain/shared/fixtures/e2e-address-book.ts) is the address-book theme's code, so it is listed as shared. Kept apart from the 'View' link and address lines row: that one changes the row's last cell and the Address column, this one changes which rows there are and how many pages; each already has enough acceptance for one sitting. Main checked at origin/main: party-picker/_address-picker.njk still renders govukPagination and the inset, and plants' three pickers now share features/address-book-picker, so the plants half is one change there. The client module that carried a tick through the pagination links goes with the pagination. Theme: consignment-parties.

rows.title: Same-as shortcuts on the roles and addresses page
rows.detail: Lets a trader fill the consignor from the place of origin, and the importer and the place of destination from the consignee, with one button press on the live-animals roles and addresses page. The consignor is often the farm of origin and the importer is usually the consignee, so today the trader picks the same address twice. The button copies the source party's record onto the notification as an independent copy, so a later change to the source does not ripple through.
acceptanceCriteria: With a place of origin chosen and no consignor, the Consignor section shows a 'Same as place of origin' button styled as a link beside its 'Add a consignor' link (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-033; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-042; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-049; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-018)

With a consignee chosen and no importer, the Importer section shows a 'Same as consignee' button styled as a link beside its 'Add an importer' link; with a consignee chosen and no place of destination, the Place of destination section shows a 'Same as consignee' button beside its 'Add a place of destination' link (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-034; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-043, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-044; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-050; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-022)

A same-as button shows only while its source party has an address and its target party has none, and the only pairs that offer one are place of origin to consignor, consignee to importer and consignee to place of destination (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-038; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-049, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-050; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-020)

Pressing a same-as button shows the roles and addresses page again with no success banner, the target section showing the source party's name and full address lines with a 'Change' link (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-035, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-036; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-045, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-046, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-047, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-048; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-051)

After a copy, changing the source party to a different address leaves the target party showing the address that was copied (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-037; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-052; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-021)

A same-as button copies the source address even when the target party's picker does not offer it, and the target section then shows that address (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-037; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-099, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-100)

The copied party's name, address lines, country, phone number and email address show for the target party on check your answers (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-036; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-085, repo-frontend-p9-086)

The same-as buttons work with JavaScript turned off, and every new string has a Welsh machine-draft counterpart (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-023; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-089)
rows.notes: Re-drafted on this re-distil from existing row inc-088; no requirement behind it changed in substance. Combines the three same-as buttons and their shared show and copy rules: one page form, one copy behaviour, one set of tests. 'Section' means the page's headed party section: on origin/main the roles and addresses page builds each section in addresses/controller.js sections() as a hubSection with an addLink or a chosen address, and template.njk renders them outside the page's form, which wraps only the save actions. So a 'Same as ...' button beside a section's add link needs the form widened to hold the sections, or a form of its own carrying the crumb and the concurrency token, and the button added through the section object rather than the template alone. c-100: DR1's collision block does not hold this back. The prototype's same-as action value is not adopted (req-1829, out of scope): the button posts the real service's own fields. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm leaves high-risk plants unchanged here: plants has no roles and addresses page to carry the shortcut. Order: build after the role-filtered pickers row, because the 'copies even when the target's picker does not offer it' criterion needs role-carrying records; on the compose stack that record is set-up for a one-page assertion, which the test rules allow. Main checked at origin/main: no same-as shortcut exists (addresses/controller.js partySectionBuilder). Theme: consignment-parties.

rows.title: Picker 'View' link to the INS address book and back, and the picker's address lines
rows.detail: Replaces each live-animals picker row's in-place details expander with a 'View' link that opens the address in the INS address book, carrying that picker as its return, so a trader can read, correct or delete the record and come back to the picker they left. The INS frontend stays the one place an address is shown in full and the address book's only writer. On the animals and the high-risk plants pickers each address line shows on its own line, which reads more easily in a narrow column. The high-risk plants pickers are not wired to the INS address book, so they keep their in-place details disclosure.
acceptanceCriteria: Each animals picker row's last cell is a 'View' link that opens that address in the INS address book, carrying a return to the same party picker of the same notification (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-062; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-060; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-064)

On the compose stack, following a picker's 'View' link opens that address in the INS address book, and its Back link, and the return after editing or deleting the record, bring the trader back to the same party picker of the same notification (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-061; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-062; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-036, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-042)
The 'View' link has a Welsh machine-draft counterpart (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-089)

On the animals party pickers and on the high-risk plants consignor and place of destination pickers, the Address column shows each address line, town or city, county and postcode the record holds on its own line (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-060; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-066; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-061; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-011; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-038)

Each high-risk plants picker row's last cell is a 'View details' disclosure that opens in place and lists the record's name, address lines, country, phone number and email address (repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-012; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-064)
rows.notes: Re-drafted on this re-distil from existing row inc-090; neither requirement changed in substance. Combines the 'View' link with the Address column's line-per-line layout, because both change the same picker results row and the same address-line helper, so building them apart would repeat the same set-up, review and ladder. c-097: the prototype wins over the in-place expander; the tests repo's expander test (repo-tests-p5-014) changes with it. c-096: the prototype wins over the comma-joined column. The INS half is already on origin/main of the INS frontend: features/address-book/return-to.js accepts a return that is an INS path or a URL on the animals frontend's origin and refuses anything else, and the view page uses it for Back and carries it on Edit and Delete, so insfrontend is not in this row's repos and no external dependency on the address-book branch is needed for it. The builder should keep that allow-list behaviour when it sends the picker's return, so the link is no open redirect; that is a safeguard rather than a source requirement, so it is not a criterion. In stub mode, where no INS frontend runs, the fit suite observes only that the link is there with its return; where it leads is observed on the compose stack, which is why criterion 2 names it. The plants criterion is a guard that the plants pickers keep their disclosure; the plants change in this row is the address lines only, which is why plantsfrontend is in repos. The return to a germinal products picker is req-1831's concern, not this row's. CARRY OVER: the existing row inc-090 also holds req-1960 (each picker row links to its record in the INS address book and back) and a criterion from the 19 October designers review that each animals picker uses the full page width through the service's display surface; both are other areas' and this draft leaves them for the combiner to carry over with inc-090's id. Main checked at origin/main: party-picker/_cells.njk still has the pickerDetailsCell expander, wired in view-model/table-rows.js; address lines are comma-joined in animals party-picker/view-model/address-lines.js and in plants address-book-picker/address-lines.js. Theme: consignment-parties.

rows.title: The roles and addresses page shows a permanent address where one is needed, and its task completes only when every section shown does
rows.detail: Makes the live-animals roles and addresses page ask for exactly what the consignment needs and say honestly when it is done. A pet consignment that needs an animal's permanent address gets a 'Permanent address' section on the page, among the consignment's other addresses, with the link that opens the permanent address page. The overview's task then counts every section the page shows, so a cattle notification is not called complete without its CPH number and a pet notification not without its permanent address. The CPH number exemptions stay as they are: the germinal commodity codes move into their own set rather than joining the live-animals exemption list.
acceptanceCriteria: For commodity code 01061900 with at least one chosen species that needs a permanent address, the roles and addresses page shows a 'Permanent address' section with the hint 'A permanent address is where an animal:', the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-013, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-016, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-030; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-019, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-022, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-023, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-024)

The 'Permanent address' section shows only for such a consignment: every other live-animals consignment's roles and addresses page shows the five party sections and, where the consignment is in scope of one, the CPH number section (prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-019; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p14-026; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-097)

The overview's 'Roles and addresses' task does not read 'Complete' while any section the page shows is empty, and reads 'Complete' once every party has an address and the CPH number or permanent address the page asks for is given (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-039, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-040; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-080; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-004, repo-frontend-p9-028, repo-frontend-p9-175)

Following the 'Add a permanent address' link and giving the permanent address returns to the roles and addresses page, whose 'Permanent address' section then shows that address with a 'Change' link (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-030; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-026, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-027, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-028, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-029)
Every new string on the page has a Welsh machine-draft counterpart (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-089)
rows.notes: Re-drafted on this re-distil from existing row inc-096. Combines the page's permanent address section and its task completion: they share the parties obligations and the page's section list, so building them apart would build the section and then teach the task about it in a second sitting. c-104: completion counts every section the page shows. req-574 (exempt only 0101 and 01061900) is adopted as already met and its germinal half is req-1826, so no criterion names the germinal commodity codes. CHANGE ON THIS RE-DISTIL: req-582 (where 'Save and continue' goes from this page) has left this row. Its behaviour is the journey's step order, in frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow, which the split-off journey-foundation theme owns, and that theme's inc-001 already carries the same acceptance word for word ('Save and continue' on roles and addresses goes to the contact address, and to the overview when every section is complete). The existing row held req-582 with no criterion of its own for it, which is a coverage fiction; req-582 is listed in this draft's splitOff for the journey-foundation branch instead. Where the 'Add a permanent address' link leads, and the permanent address page itself, are the cph-permanent-and-contact and identification-and-permanent-address areas' work, so this row waits on the permanent address page row (inc-054) and on the CPH number page row (inc-091); criterion 4 only observes the return to this page. High-risk plants is unchanged: it has no roles and addresses page. Main checked at origin/main: the CPH half is already there, with the overview's addresses task counting the addresses page and the CPH page together in flow/task-rows.js and the CPH section showing only when in scope in addresses/controller.js; there is no permanent-address feature folder yet. Build note: template.njk renders a section's hint as one govuk-hint paragraph, so the bullets need the section object and the template to carry a list. Making the permanent address count towards the task may be done in the addresses page's own obligations, or by adding the permanent address page to the addresses task row in flow/task-rows.js, which journey-foundation owns; the first keeps the change inside this theme and is preferred. Theme: consignment-parties.

rows.title: Germinal products roles and addresses page and party pickers, with no CPH number or permanent address
rows.detail: Gives the germinal products set its own roles and addresses page and its own five party pickers, copied from the live-animals addresses feature once this programme has built it, under the germinal set's own journey and routes with the live-animals slugs. The copy behaves and reads as the live-animals page and pickers do, so a trader importing germinal products records every party of the consignment within the germinal notification. Germinal products are not kept on a holding and are not pets, so the germinal set is only ever asked for the five consignment addresses: it shows no CPH number section and no permanent address section, and serves neither page.
acceptanceCriteria: For every germinal commodity, the germinal products set's roles and addresses page shows exactly five sections, in this order: Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-014; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-122; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-017, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-018, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-057)

The germinal products set serves no CPH number page and no permanent address page: nothing on its pages links to one, and opening either page's address under a germinal products notification shows 'Page not found' (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-017, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-018; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-019)

Each germinal section's hint reads as on the live-animals page, word for word, including Place of origin 'The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain' and Place of destination 'This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address.' (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-014; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-122-m1; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-046)

Each empty germinal section's link ('Add a place of origin', 'Add a consignor', 'Add a consignee', 'Add an importer', 'Add a place of destination') opens the germinal set's own picker for that party; choosing an address there and saving returns to the germinal roles and addresses page, which shows the full address with a 'Change' link, and the address is saved on that germinal products notification only (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-009, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-011; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-001, repo-frontend-p9-046)

The germinal pickers behave as the live-animals pickers do: the same role filtering on one page, the same server search, the same 'View' link, the same address lines, the same results count and the same behaviour on saving (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-013, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-014)

The germinal roles and addresses page offers the same-as buttons ('Same as place of origin' on Consignor, 'Same as consignee' on Importer and on Place of destination) under the same rules as the live-animals page (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-014)

The germinal overview's 'Roles and addresses' task reads 'Complete' once all five parties have an address, with no CPH number and no permanent address asked for (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-014; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-017, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-018)

In Welsh the germinal roles and addresses page and its pickers show the same Welsh text as the live-animals ones, and they have no serious or critical accessibility violations (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-014; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-089)
rows.notes: Re-drafted on this re-distil from existing row inc-181; neither requirement changed in substance. Combines req-1826 (five sections only, no CPH number and no permanent address) and req-1827 (the germinal set's own copy of the page and the pickers), because they are one page and one copy: building the copy without its section rule would show a CPH row the set cannot answer. c-091: ruling sam-2026-10-09 makes germinal products its own set whose pages are copies of their live-animals feature folders, and calls that duplication accepted and desired; it splits req-574 so the germinal half sits here. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-p1-014 says each germinal page is copied after this programme has built its live twin, so this row lands after every buildable live-animals row of this area; the germinal-products theme already depends on the consignment-parties theme, so that order holds through the themes. It never waits on the blocked filter-as-you-type row: that row changes the germinal pickers too when it builds. The routes and form fields stay the real service's, with the live-animals slugs (req-1828 already met, req-1829 out of scope). Same behaviour in stub mode and on the compose stack, as for the live-animals pickers. CARRY OVER: the existing row inc-181 also holds req-1832, req-1833 and req-1840 and their criteria, from the cph-permanent-and-contact and notification-hub areas, including the germinal overview's 'Consignment parties' section and its single 'Roles and addresses' row; the combiner should keep them there with inc-181's id, text and theme, and take out the repeats this draft's criteria 2 and 7 make. Observable only once the germinal set's own mount, journey and overview exist, which is why inc-181 depends on the germinal mount row and on the live CPH and permanent address rows. Theme: germinal-products.

rows.title: Party pickers filter as the trader types
rows.detail: With JavaScript, narrows a party picker's one-page list as the trader types, with no page reload, on both animals sets' five pickers and on the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, so a trader with a long address book finds the right record without a round trip. The place of origin picker narrows by country as well, as the trader types or picks one. It waits on design: until design, with the product owner, answers the open question on live filtering, the server search behind the submitting search button is the whole search. It is built as design answers, or dropped if design drops it.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript on, typing in the search box of a live-animals or germinal products party picker shows, with no page reload, only the rows whose name, address lines or country contain the typed text, ignoring case, and the results count shows how many are on screen (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-057; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-074, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-075, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-076; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-054; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-067)

The high-risk plants consignor and place of destination pickers narrow the same way as the trader types (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-050, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-042; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-004)

With JavaScript on, typing in or picking a country on the place of origin picker shows, with no page reload, only the rows whose country contains the typed text or exactly matches the picked country, on both animals sets (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-055; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-055, repo-frontend-p9-070; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-070)
Clearing the search box shows every row of the role's list again, and the results count returns to the full total (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-102)

With JavaScript turned off, each picker's submitting search button still narrows the list on the server, as it does today (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-066; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-070)
openQuestions: Design, with the product owner, must answer the open question on filtering a list as the trader types before this builds; if design drops it, this row is dropped. Until then the server search behind each picker's submitting search button is the whole search (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-052, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-053, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-063, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-067).

Design must also answer the open question on the place of origin picker's filtering as the trader types, which goes to the product owner alongside the one above (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-070).
rows.notes: Re-drafted on this re-distil from existing row inc-193. Both requirements still carry a blocker, so the row stays blocked. Combines the four party pickers' filter and the place of origin picker's country filter, because ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm puts them in one waiting-on-design increment and they are one client module on one results table. Client-side code is new: neither frontend's picker carries JavaScript today. Depends on the role-filtered pickers row (one page to filter, and the results count it updates) and on the germinal set's pickers, because req-592 names both animals sets. CARRY OVER: the existing row inc-193 also holds req-2039 (the INS address book list re-requesting itself as the trader types), the address-book-list area's, and the insfrontend repo key with it; this draft leaves both for the combiner to carry over with inc-193's id. Build note: the animals transporter list already filters as you type, with shared accent-folding and bold-match helpers under frontend:src/client/common/helpers; build the picker filter from those rather than a new one. In plants the three pickers share features/address-book-picker, so one change covers the consignor, place of destination and contact pickers. The transporter list's own in-page filter is not this row's. Theme: waiting-on-design.

splitOff.why: It changes the address book's own record and list: roles on each address record and a role-scoped, unpaginated list of an organisation's addresses. That code is addressbook:src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/addressbook/address, which the split-off address-book theme owns, and that theme's own row inc-059 (still todo) already builds the typed record there for req-1256. On origin/main Address.java is documented as 'an untyped, organisation-owned address-book entry' and AddressRequest refuses a type, so nothing in this area's code can meet it. The frontend half of the requirement, each picker asking for its own role, is stated again by req-608 and stays in this area's role-filtered pickers row.

It changes where 'Save and continue' goes from the roles and addresses page on the opening run: to the contact address page, or to the overview when every section is complete. That is the journey's step order, in frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow, which the split-off journey-foundation theme owns; the roles and addresses page itself only calls the flow for its next target. That theme's row inc-001 already carries the same acceptance word for word, including the opening run going to the contact address and the overview shortcut when everything is complete, and its inc-002 carries the return to the overview from a page opened by its task.
